Security Goals
▐CIA Triad: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability
UNIT 01
Confidentiality
Integrity
Availability
●preserves authorized 
restrictions on information 
access and disclosure.
●protects personal privacy 
and proprietary records from 
unauthorized reading.
●guards against improper 
information modification or 
destruction.
●ensures that data and 
programs change only in a 
specified and authorized 
manner.
●ensures timely and reliable 
access to and use of 
information.
●guarantees that systems 
work promptly and service is 
not denied to authorized 
users.

▐Other Goals: Accountability, Authenticity, and Reliability
UNIT 01
Accountability
Authenticity
Reliability
●requires that the actions of 
an entity be traced uniquely 
to that specific entity.
●supports deterrence, fault 
isolation, intrusion detection, 
and forensic analysis.
●property of being genuine, 
verifiable, and trusted.
●provides confidence in the

message, or a message 
originator.
●ensures that a system 
performs its intended 
function in an unimpaired 
manner without accidental 
failures.
●uses formal IT security 
management processes to 
preserve consistent system 
operations.

base_slide.title: Security Goals
base_slide.text:
Security Goals
UNIT 01
Example
Alice launches an online store called “Alice’s 
Market (AM).” Bob visits the website, creates 
an account, and decides to buy a T-shirt. He 
enters his credit card number to complete the 
purchase. Meanwhile, Trudy happens to 
discover the store and begins thinking about 
how to attack it.
Question: What are Alice’s and Bob’s 
security concerns? How might Trudy 
view the situation?
Confidentiality
Only authorized parties can access Bob’s personal and 
payment information.
Integrity
Bob’s order and payment details remain accurate and 
unchanged.
Availability
Alice’s Market remains accessible when Bob wants to 
shop.
Trudy may try to steal Bob’s information, alter his order, or make the store unavailable.

Accountability
Every action on Alice's Market is logged so that Bob's 
purchase or Trudy's attempted attack can be uniquely traced 
back to the responsible party.
Authenticity
Alice's Market correctly verifies that the person logging into 
the account and making the purchase is genuinely Bob and 
not Trudy.
Reliability
Alice's Market processes Bob's transaction consistently and 
operates properly without any accidental system failures.

base_slide.title: Attack Surfaces and Attack Trees
base_slide.text:
Attack Surfaces and Attack Trees
▐Structure of Attack Trees
●An attack tree lays out how a goal can be reached. 
●The root node represents the ultimate goal of the attacker.
●Each level breaks the goal into finer sub-goals, representing different ways to achieve it.
●The leaf nodes are the concrete, actionable attacks at the bottom of the tree.

base_slide.text:
Attack Surfaces and Attack Trees
▐Relations
●Each node other than a leaf is either an AND-node or an OR-node.
●It determines what the attacker must achieve.
●For AND-node, the sub-goals represented by all of that node’s sub-nodes must be achieved.
●For OR-node, at least one of the sub-goals must be achieved.

base_slide.text:
WEEK 01.
Key Takeaways
Cybersecurity protects digital systems and assets in adversarial environments.
The CIA triad—confidentiality, integrity, and availability—defines the fundamental goals of 
cybersecurity.
Effective security reduces risk by identifying assets, threats, vulnerabilities, attack surfaces, and 
appropriate countermeasures.
